name: SEC EDGAR (US SEC)
why: Free, no key, JSON APIs; full-text search since 2001, filing index back to 1993. 8-K Item 1.01/2.01, S-4, SC TO-T, DEFM14A give reliable, dated M&A labels for US-listed acquirers, including their Asian targets.
risk: US-centric; needs filing-text parsing; 10 req/s limit.
action: Build ETL first; use as the gold-standard label set for the model.

name: EDINET API v2 (Japan FSA)
why: Free API key. Annual / semi-annual / quarterly reports viewable 10 years; extraordinary reports 臨時報告書 (M&A / business-transfer disclosures with target name, financials and consideration above 15% of net assets), tender-offer filings and 5% reports viewable 5 years (FIEA Art. 25, 27-14, 27-28, verified). Statutory public data under public-data terms of use.
risk: No source, free or paid, holds more than 5 years of Japanese M&A filings, so history must be accumulated by archiving from now. Scraping / mass access prohibited by terms (API use is the sanctioned route, about 1 request per second).
action: Start a daily archiver immediately; back-fill the 10-year list window on day one.

name: OpenDART (Korea FSS) + TWSE OpenAPI/MOPS (Taiwan) + HKEXnews (HK)
why: OpenDART: free REST API with key, disclosures from 1999, corporate use not prohibited. TWSE OpenAPI free. HKEXnews harvestable (no official API).
risk: Korean/Chinese-language documents; HKEX has no official free API (harvesting only); redistribution limits.
action: Add as second-wave ETL after EDGAR/EDINET.

name: Mergr
why: About 225k human-researched M&A/PE transactions with buyers, targets, advisors. Pro seat USD 150/month publicly priced; Data Direct API + bulk CSV is a separate quote. Owns 100% of its data, so training rights are more negotiable than for aggregators.
cost: USD 1,800/yr per seat; Data Direct quote (inferred low-to-mid)
risk: History depth not published; US/Europe PE-heavy, thinner Asia SME coverage; ML rights unknown.
action: Trial Pro; request Data Direct quote with explicit internal-model-training clause.

name: Tracxn
why: 226k+ acquisitions, 7.7M companies, strong India/SEA/China startup coverage. API (Postman docs) plus data dumps and custom dataset packs priced by number of unique companies, not seats. Free Lite tier for evaluation.
cost: Quote only; inferred mid for a scoped data pack
risk: Startup/tech-skewed, weak on traditional Japanese SMEs; history inferred from ~2010s; ML rights unknown.
action: Evaluate on Lite; request Data Solutions quote for an Asia acquisitions pack.

name: TDnet paid data (JPX): TDnet on Snowflake / TDnet API / TDnetDBS
why: Timely-disclosure feed where Japanese M&A, TOB and business-transfer announcements first appear. Snowflake-native delivery from about JPY 100,000/month; API JPY 70,000/month base plus tiered document fees; TDnetDBS is the historical archive.
risk: Free site keeps only 31 days; archive start date must be requested; terms distinguish internal use vs redistribution.
action: Request TDnetDBS back-file scope and the terms document; confirm internal analytics/model use.

name: Coresignal
why: Published data dictionary includes funding rounds, acquired-by, acquisition lists, IPO fields and up to 8 years of monthly headcount for 11M+ companies. Public pricing USD 49-5,000/month, Elite about USD 54k/yr; bulk Parquet/JSONL to S3; markets itself for AI training.
risk: LinkedIn-derived; Japan SME coverage thinner than TSR/TDB; training rights sit in a separate signed data licence.
action: Buy a small tier to test Asia coverage; negotiate dataset licence with training clause.

name: Diffbot Knowledge Graph
why: 246M organisations with acquiredBy/isAcquired/parent fields; REST + DQL + Bulk Extract API. Fully public pricing: Startup USD 299/month, Plus USD 899/month. Terms of Use explicitly allow using generated facts in commercial applications (most permissive found).
risk: Snapshot only: stores the most recent acquirer, so poor as a historical label source; web-extracted quality varies for Asian SMEs.
action: Use for entity resolution and feature enrichment, not for labels.

name: Tokyo Shoko Research (TSR) bulk file + API service
role: Japan SME universe and target-scoring features (low-mid)
why: 10M+ Japanese companies including SMEs. Published bulk pricing: base fee JPY 50k-300k per delivery plus about JPY 15-23 per company at volume (100k companies about USD 12k). API exists with free test environment (XML/PDF).
risk: Only about 3 fiscal years per company; historical panel needs custom arrangement; per-purpose licence means training use must be agreed explicitly.
action: Request layout spec and quote for a 100k-company extract with derived-use rights.

name: ITjuzi (IT桔子)
why: Chinese primary-market and M&A data since 2013; enterprise service explicitly offers API and bulk CSV/MySQL/JSON delivery with incremental refresh. Individual membership CNY 798/yr.
cost: CNY 798/yr individual; enterprise API/bulk quote (inferred low-mid)
risk: Chinese-language; China cross-border data-transfer rules need qualified legal review; ML rights unknown.
action: Request enterprise data-service quote; legal check on data export.

name: SPEEDA + SPEEDA RECOF (Uzabase)
role: Japan/Asia deal database with 1985+ Recof history (mid)
why: 1.9M+ M&A records; SPEEDA RECOF inherits the Recof Japanese deal series from 1985. Enterprise tier includes API and is described as supporting integration with internal generative-AI systems. Third-party prices: Basic about JPY 55k/month, Professional about JPY 110k/month.
cost: About JPY 0.7M-1.3M/yr per ID (third-party, unconfirmed); Enterprise/API quote
risk: Much content is licensed in (Recof, Euromonitor), so training rights likely restricted; API is an enrichment/CRM integration API rather than a bulk research API.
action: Request Enterprise quote specifically for SPEEDA RECOF bulk export and model-training rights.

name: MARR Pro (Recof Data)
role: Japan deal database, canonical 1985+ series (quote only)
why: Successor to the discontinued Recof M&A Database (service ended about spring 2026); 80,000+ Japanese deals since 1985 with scheme detail; Excel bulk download. MARR Online (JPY 16,500-82,500/yr) is only the editorial portal.
risk: No API; Excel export only; small publisher, systematic extraction/training likely outside standard terms.
action: Ask Recof Data for a one-time historical data licence rather than seats.

name: DeepSearch Finorma (Korea)
role: Korean company + deal data via LLM-oriented API (quote only)
why: REST API marketed as a corporate/financial data API for LLMs; 1.5M private companies; 10 years of financials; DART/KRX disclosures from 1999. Vendor posture is the most AI-friendly in the Asia group.
risk: Korea only; no public pricing; training rights unknown.

name: Event Registry (newsapi.ai)
why: REST API with event extraction; archive since 2014; public tiers from USD 90/month (5K tokens). Useful for weak signals (management change, distress, strategic review) ahead of a deal.
risk: Token multiplier for historical years pushes cost up; storing full article text for training likely restricted.
action: Use for derived features/events only, not raw text storage.

name: Crunchbase, CB Insights, AlphaSense/Tegus, J-Quants retail API, Proxycurl, GDELT, Grata, Sourcescrub
why: Crunchbase ToS prohibit training models on its content (API/data licence quote about USD 20k+/yr anyway). CB Insights MSA explicitly bans use in training models/algorithms. AlphaSense/Tegus ToU ban use with AI/ML tools. J-Quants retail API is individuals-only (use J-Quants Pro instead, published per-dataset internal-use pricing). Proxycurl shut down July 2025. GDELT has no M&A event category. Grata/Sourcescrub have no Japan/Asia coverage.
risk: Contract breach if used for training without a negotiated carve-out.
action: Only revisit with a written data-licensing agreement that names internal model training.

name: Moody's Orbis M&A (ex-Zephyr), PitchBook, S&P Capital IQ Pro, LSEG Deals/SDC, Mergermarket, FactSet, Bloomberg, Preqin, AVCJ, Wind
why: Deepest histories (Orbis M&A from 1997 EU / 2001 US; SDC from the 1970s-80s), full advisors/multiples/rationale, and formal data-licensing programmes that can carve out ML training. All quote-only and inferred above USD 50k/yr with API or feed rights. Orbis M&A is the strongest single option for Japanese private-company depth if budget later allows.
risk: Cost; seat-only subscriptions never permit training.
action: If budget grows, request a scoped Japan+APAC historical bulk extract from Moody's rather than platform seats.
